**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2022/10/29 (Sat) 15:29  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Definition of a non-deterministic logical matrix: a tuple $(X, Y, V, C, \cdot)$, where $X$ is a set of truth-values, $Y \subseteq X$ is a set of designated truth-values, $V$ is a set of propositions, $C$ is a set of logical connectives, and $\cdot: V \cup C \rightarrow \mathcal{P}(X)$ assigns a set of truth-values in $X$ to each proposition in $V$ and logical connective in $C$.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Example of a non-deterministic matrix using 3 values (1, 2, 3) with (2, 3) designated, and the only connective being negation with paraconsistent behavior:  
* $X = {1, 2, 3}$  
* $Y = {2, 3}$  
* $V = {\text{p}, \text{q}}$  
* $C = {\neg}$  
* $\cdot(\text{p}) = {2, 3}$  
* $\cdot(\text{q}) = {2, 3}$  
* $\cdot(\neg\text{p}) = {1, 2, 3}$  
* $\cdot(\neg\text{q}) = {1, 2, 3}$  
[USER] Expressed dissatisfaction with the definition of Non-Deterministic Matrix, stating it does not take into account the arity of the connectives.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Revised definition of a non-deterministic logical matrix to include arity:  
* $\cdot: C \times X^{arity} \rightarrow \mathcal{P}(X)$ assigns a set of truth-values to each logical connective in $C$ and a tuple of truth-values in $X$.  
[USER] Requested an example of a Revised Non-Deterministic Matrix.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided an example of a revised non-deterministic matrix:  
* $X = {1, 2, 3}$  
* $Y = {2, 3}$  
* $V = {\text{p}, \text{q}}$  
* $C = {\neg, \text{and}}$  
* $arity(\neg) = 1$  
* $arity(\text{and}) = 2$  
* $\cdot(\neg, 1) = {2, 3}$  
* $\cdot(\neg, 2) = {1, 3}$  
* $\cdot(\neg, 3) = {
